metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.7) after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >+10% above 30-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates true volatility; add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating ±0.5+ or recent 3-day std dev > 2.5).
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3–0.5), model tends to lag 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if price is trending upward or 1–2 days back if downward.
